questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not to far away from home, easy to interact with locals in terms of language, university located close to both nature and city life, kind of similar culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, except the information about courses (because of outdated course catalog)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received all relevant information through emails

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Was easy since there is a housing guarantee through the student welfare organisation Sammen. But mind that you most likely have to share a small room with a roommate and share kitchen with several others; however this is a great opportunity to meet new people

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's still easy to get to campus by public transportation. It's nice to live a bit away from campus since it's closer to natural areas

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course catalog was outdated, so I couldn't take the courses I originally planned to take. I ended up having to take a course in Norwegian

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration is through the Student Web. There're both open and restricted courses. The restricted courses you have to apply for a bit earlier I think

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get emails and there's information on the university's website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that the course catalog is updated e.g. by sending an email to the host institution. Remember to check the timetable and exam dates of all the courses you plan to take

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were only two courses available for bachelor students in economics even though my exchange spot was specifically for economics students. Therefore, I had to take a third course together with the local students in Norwegian

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two of the courses were together with 1st semester students, so they were not academically challenging since I'm in my 5th semester

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much less teaching than at UCPH. Seminars instead of class teaching, but the seminars were kinda like class teaching

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON115 Development Economics I, ECON260 Industrial Organization and Competition Policy, ECON116 Miljø- og Ressursøkonomi

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON260 Industrial Organization and Competition Policy was the most challenging and interesting. Great if you are interested in microeconomics, game theory and markets with only a few firms

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to buy a lot of practical stuff like hiking shoes, backpack etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is very expensive, but public transportion is much cheaper than in Denmark. Food prices are also high, but kinda similar compared to prices in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to go to a tryout to get a spot on their sport teams. There're only a few spots so it's rather difficult

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of sports, outdoor and academic organizations available, but I didn't take part in any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go on hikes and explore the nature. Also great opportunity to go on short trips to other places/cities in Norway. I went to both Voss and Tromsø

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city center (Bryggen, Fish Market etc), Nordnes (viewpoint), Fløibanen, Fjord Cruise, Gamlehaugen, Fantoft Stavkirke, KODE museums, christmas market, plenty of great bakeries and cafes (Solros, Nobel Bopel, Godt Brød, Baker Brun, Blom etc.)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy since it's not that different from the Danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the mentor week, events and student organizations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love for nature and going on hikes

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Live at a student housing cause this makes it a lot easier to meet new people and create relations
2) Go on trips to explore other parts of Norway and especially the beautiful nature
3) Participate as much as possible to get the most out of the exchange

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that the courses you want to take are offered during your semester

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new relationships with people from all around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative work (was mostly before the exchange)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
